Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Attached is our marked-up version with legal's comments — see the pricing exhibit (pages 4-6) where we've added language about a floor and a rolling cap on credits. Two items we need you to clarify:

- How will the floor interact with tiered discounts if our usage dips below the minimum in a given month? We want predictable true-ups, not retroactive discounts.
- The redline includes a cap on cumulative credits; however, procurement is asking for a clearer definition of how "cumulative" is calculated across quarters and what triggers a cap reset.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept: (a) a quarterly true-up (instead of monthly) and (b) explicit language that any credits applied are capped per contract year?

Karthik / Sofia — I reviewed the markup and drafted a couple of options below to keep negotiations moving. High level: we can do quarterly true-ups but need a clean floor calculation and a cap that limits downside for Redwood. Proposed bullets for Exhibit A redline: 

1) Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC): BrightArc will commit to a MMC of X tokens/month. For the quarter, the MMC-quarterly floor equals sum(MMC_months).

2) Quarterly True-Up: If actual usage for a quarter is below the MMC-quarterly floor, BrightArc will be invoiced/credited via a single quarterly true-up. Credits applied will not be refundable and will be applied against future invoices in that contract year.

3) Cumulative Credit Cap: Credits applied in any contract year are capped at 20% of the annual committed spend. Cap resets on the contract anniversary.

4) Tiered Discounts: Discount tiers remain based on monthly consumption bands. If usage in a month falls below the MMC, the monthly tier for that month will not retroactively apply; tiers for subsequent months are unaffected.

5) Audit/Visibility: Redwood will provide token-level usage exports to support the quarterly reconciliation.

Snippet to drop into Exhibit A (plain text attached): exhibitA_pricing_snippet.txt

If legal wants different wording, Marissa can propose redline language. If BrightArc prefers a minimum commitment rather than an MMC formula, we can propose a two-tier minimum (lower MMC with a higher annual true-up).

Let me know if you want me to push a specific numeric MMC for modeling; otherwise I'll wait for Sofia's input.

Neha Kapoor

Karthik / Neha — thanks for the quick responses. Procurement has discussed the MMC + quarterly true-up approach. A couple of items from our side:

- We cannot accept a cap that is expressed as a percent of "annual committed spend" without a clear definition of committed spend (is it net of discounts? does it include overages?). Please clarify the base.
- We are hesitant about credits being non-refundable; procurement wants the option of a refund for unused pre-paid credits at year-end or conversion to a credit for the next year.

As an alternative, we've proposed the attached: minimum monthly commitment of 60% of expected baseline, quarterly true-up, and a rolling quarterly cap reset (instead of annual reset). See BrightArc_alternative_terms.docx.

We need a firm position by EOD Friday to meet our internal procurement timeline. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept either (A) refundability for unused pre-paid credits up to 10% of annual committed spend, or (B) switch the cap reset to quarterly with a lower per-quarter cap?

Thanks,
Jake Turner
Procurement Manager | BrightArc Analytics

Jake / Sofia — appreciate the candor and the alternative language. After discussing with pricing and contracts, here's a compromise we can accept to close the order this week: 

- MMC: We'll set an explicit MMC (numeric value to be inserted after your confirmation of baseline). The quarterly-floor equals the sum of the three monthly MMCs.
- Quarterly True-Up: Agreed. Reconciliations happen once per quarter.
- Credit Treatment: We can allow refundable credits up to 10% of annual committed spend OR conversion to next-year credit, your choice, provided the refund request is made within 30 days of the contract anniversary.
- Credit Cap & Reset: We'll cap credits at 15% of annual committed spend with a quarterly assessment that allows unused credit carry-forward, but resets on contract anniversary. If you prefer a rolling quarterly reset instead, we can model that but it will increase unit prices slightly (we can provide numbers).
- Tiered Discounts: No retroactive re-tiering for months that fall below MMC; tiers apply prospectively.

Next steps: if BrightArc confirms (a) which credit option you prefer (refund vs carry-forward) and (b) baseline number for MMC, we will circulate a final redline and a DocuSign link for signature.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.example/brightarc_offer

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if it helps.

Best,
